priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v27 REJECT, whose sole SHOULD-FIX named the Authenticode order/specification divergence. v28 applies both remedies I offered — the section walk and a specificationGoverns precedence clause — which is the strongest possible invitation to a confirmatory read. I therefore re-derived the algorithm check against the Authenticode procedure itself rather than against my own prior wording, and I confirm it below as fully repaired. blockers.appliesTo: PTCB-V27-B2 — the boot-time half is genuinely closed; the bind still attests a boot-time fact while declaring a run-time subject
blockers.title: measuredBootBind proves which kernel the firmware boot manager launched at boot, but the subject it populates is running-kernel-package and nothing binds the running kernel to the booted one, so a post-boot kernel replacement is attested as the running kernel
blockers.whatIsGenuinelyClosed: I want the scale of this generation's work on record, because the boot-time chain is now excellent and I could not break it. trustedHandoff replaces v27's asserted StartImage fact with observable evidence: BootCurrent and the Boot#### load-option bytes are retained; filePathList MUST equal kernelEvent.devicePath; callingFromBootOption must be the TCG PC Client action string at exactly kernelEvent.logIndex minus 1, with 'Any other distance refuses'; noInterveningApplication forbids any other EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION between that action and the first PCR-4 separator; preKernelReferences requires every PCR-0/1/2/4 code-bearing event before the kernel to appear exactly once and match a signed TCB allowlist member. The quote now covers PCR 0,1,2,4,7 with a composite pcrDigest computed in ascending index order and compared to TPMS_ATTEST.attested.quote.pcrDigest, magic and type validated, extraData equal to the nonce, the AK Name derived from the retained TPMT_PUBLIC and compared to qualifiedSigner, and a four-field signedEntry binding the AK certificate. Codex's sentence 'the verifier must distinguish LoadImage(K)-then-run(M) from LoadImage(K)-then-StartImage(K)' is answered for the firmware phase. My concern is a different phase.
blockers.theGap: Every element above is evidence about what happened before the first PCR-4 EV_SEPARATOR. The quote's freshness proves the quote was produced during this qualification run — the nonce binds runIdentity, observedAt, subject, signedCarrierDigest and a 32-byte verifier challenge — but the PCR values it attests are boot-time contents. A TPM PCR cannot be reset without a platform reset, and a post-boot kernel transition performed by the running OS extends nothing into PCR 4 by default. So after such a transition the retained event log still replays to the same PCR 0,1,2,4,7 values, the composite still matches, the AK signature still verifies, the nonce is still fresh, and every clause in enforcedBootPolicy still holds — while a different kernel is executing. The contract carries no run-time continuity element of any kind: I searched the whole 180484-byte artifact and found zero occurrences of kexec, lockdown, continuity, since boot, boot_id, reboot, uptime, or replacement.
blockers.whyItIsAnOverclaimRatherThanAScopeChoice: subjectByScheme.package-db declares 'kind: exactly running-kernel-package' with 'digest: 64-hex lowercase sha-256 of the running-kernel package bytes', and pathlessObservation.subject MUST equal that object. The contract therefore asserts the running kernel package, not the booted one. It never says 'booted kernel' anywhere — that phrase has zero occurrences — and neither inScopeBootConfigs, refusesBootConfigs nor unavailableRefuses mentions any post-boot condition; all three enumerate firmware, Secure Boot, event-log and device-path conditions only. A reader of this profile would reasonably conclude the bind establishes the currently running kernel, and it does not.
blockers.whyTheAdversaryIsInScope: This is not an adversary the contract has declined to model. excludesSyntheticExtend exists specifically to defeat 'An OS-time or post-separator PCR-4 extend', so an OS-time adversary is inside the threat model by the contract's own construction. That same adversary is the one who performs a post-boot kernel transition. The contract also removes the one mechanism that could have covered the interval: notThisProfile lists IMA-appraisal, and measuredBootProcedureRef repeats that IMA file measurement is not this bind. Excluding IMA is defensible on its own terms — I agreed with it at v24 — but it means nothing in this contract observes the kernel after the separator.
blockers.failureScenario: An in-scope machine qualifies exactly as specified: UEFI firmware with TPM 2.0, Secure Boot enabled, boot manager launches BootCurrent whose FilePathList is the EFI-stub kernel image K, K is measured into PCR 4 immediately after the Calling action, every pre-kernel event matches a signed TCB member, and K's Authenticode image digest equals authenticatedKernelMember.peCoffImageDigest for a member of the authenticated package. After boot, the running system transitions to a different kernel image M — under Secure Boot the platform will typically require M to be signature-verified, so M is a different but validly signed kernel, for instance an older build with a known local-privilege-escalation defect. No PCR is reset and nothing is extended. The qualification run then executes the ceremony: the retained log replays to the same PCR 0,1,2,4,7 values, the fresh quote over those PCRs verifies under the AK, the composite matches, the device-path and adjacency checks pass against the boot-time log, and the profile qualifies with subject kind running-kernel-package naming K's package. The attestation names K while M runs. Nothing in the contract detects it, and no clause refuses.
blockers.severityRationale: This is not fail-closed. Every prior finding I filed on this axis was either an unsatisfiable equality or an over-refusal; this one produces a positive, verifiable attestation of a kernel that is not running. It is the same defect class the row has been working through since v22 — evidence that is not about the executing code — surviving at the one layer no generation has yet addressed, and it is rated the way that class has been rated every prior round.
blockers.requiredRepair: Either route closes it, and both are cheap. (1) Constrain the interval: require the platform to demonstrate that no post-boot kernel transition has occurred — for example by requiring kernel lockdown in integrity mode with any kernel-replacement path restricted to signature-verified images AND a retained run-time indicator binding the running kernel identity to kernelEvent, refusing when that indicator is unavailable, in the same fail-closed style as unavailableRefuses. (2) Narrow the claim to what is proven: redefine the subject kind from running-kernel-package to the kernel image the firmware boot manager launched for this boot, state expressly in inScopeBootConfigs and unavailableRefuses that the bind does not cover post-boot kernel replacement, and record that limitation where NT-TCB-1 and g22.testMatrix can see it, exactly as the boot-configuration narrowing was disclosed at v27. Keep trustedHandoff, preKernelReferences, the composite quote, the AK Name join and nonceBind verbatim — they are correct.

repairsVerified.finding: CLAUDE-V27-S1 (mine) / PTCB-V27-S1 — enumerated order was a linear pass, not the Authenticode algorithm it named
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, with both remedies I offered and more. specificationGoverns now reads 'Where the enumerated steps are silent or differ from that specification, the specification governs. This is the same supersession form as authenticatedManifest.uniqueness', which is the precedence sentence in the form I suggested. The order is also completed rather than left to the precedence clause: step 5 now hashes through SizeOfHeaders, step 6 collects IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER entries, sorts by ascending PointerToRawData, refuses overlapping raw ranges and skips SizeOfRawData 0, step 7 hashes exactly SizeOfRawData bytes at PointerToRawData accumulating SUM_OF_BYTES_HASHED, and step 9 handles the overlay while stating 'Do not hash inter-section gaps that no section raw range covers' — which is precisely the divergence I identified. A new parse clause adds the PE32/PE32+ bounds and malformed-input refusals Codex asked for, including Magic other than 0x10B or 0x20B, NumberOfSections overrun, SizeOfHeaders overrun or undersize, and a Security directory that overruns or wraps. notThis now names the v27 defect explicitly. Test vectors are RESERVED to G22 with six named required classes including the adversarial ones; that is a disclosed routing to the qualification harness rather than a silent omission, and I do not charge it.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V27-B1 — a held descriptor fixes pathname replacement but does not freeze archive bytes
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, and I could not break it. archiveSnapshot runs before headerBind on both branches: openat the source O_NOFOLLOW, memfd_create with MFD_ALLOW_SEALING, copy every byte with the copied count required to equal fstat st_size and any short copy or read error refusing, lseek 0, then F_ADD_SEALS with F_SEAL_WRITE|F_SEAL_GROW|F_SEAL_SHRINK|F_SEAL_SEAL where failure refuses, close the source with 'publisherArchivePath is not used again', close every writable duplicate retaining only O_RDONLY descriptors, and 'all later stages (headerBind, digest, verify, extract) MUST use only snapFd'. notThis names the v27 defect in its own words: 'a held O_RDONLY descriptor on publisherArchivePath. That pins an inode against rename and does not freeze bytes.' The sealed identity {dev, ino, size, sha256} is bound to authenticityCore.payload.digest.

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V27-B3 — pathless events must retain a consumption record the closed schema forbade
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED. Both records are now single top-level event members, required on both linux-file-backed and linux-pathless, branch-gated and mutually exclusive, and each states 'This field is a top-level event member only; it MUST NOT appear inside objectAuthenticityBindRecord.' I confirmed the nested duplicates are gone: neither tag carries a materializedFileIdentity or descriptorConsumptionRecord key any more. The associationToken derivation Codex required for the no-openedObjectObservation case is present — 'associationToken MUST equal this event runIdentity plus observedAt. When the tag is linux-file-backed that same value MUST equal openedObjectObservation.associationToken' — which restores one placement while keeping the file-backed equality. Both records gained snapshotKind pinned to memfd-sealed and a seals list pinned to the four seals, and descriptorConsumptionRecord.stages is now exactly [snapshot, headerBind, digest, verify, extract].

repairsVerified.finding: PTCB-V27-S2 — retained quote, AK join and nonce omitted the operations needed for one reproducible verification
repairsVerified.result: REPAIRED, every element. akJoin now specifies exact TPMS_ATTEST parsing and validation: magic TPM_GENERATED_VALUE, type TPM_ST_ATTEST_QUOTE, extraData equal to the nonce, attested.quote.pcrSelect equal to the declared selection, and pcrDigest equal to the composite. The composite is defined in TPM selection order — 'SHA-256 of the reconstructed SHA-256 PCR values in ascending PCR index order: PCR0||PCR1||PCR2||PCR4||PCR7' — with 'There are no retained per-PCR quoted values', which removes the v27 ambiguity. The AK TPMT_PUBLIC is retained, its Name derived as the nameAlg hash and compared to qualifiedSigner, and TPMT_SIGNATURE verified under that public key. akCertificateMember is a four-field signedEntry with 'A three-field form refuses.' nonceBind gains lengthCap requiring every u16be-framed component to be at most 65535 bytes with longer values refusing, and subjectJson pins RFC 8259 canonical JSON with compact separators, fixed key order, extras rejected and minimal escaping.

limitsOfThisReview: I reviewed the five claimed repairs, the expanded measured-boot and RPM surfaces, the closed change roster, the pin chain, the live register/COORD/file-04 carries and the authority refusals. Paths outside this round's roster were checked only for unchangedness. CLAUDE-V28-B1 rests on the documented behaviour of TPM PCRs — that they cannot be reset without a platform reset and are extended only when something extends them — and on the contract's own text, not on execution against live firmware. The repair I specify does not require conceding any technical point, since narrowing the declared subject to the booted kernel resolves the overclaim regardless.
summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at dd9f4376... and 0444 at both ends, HEAD steady, 37/37 chain pins reproduce, both frozen v27 verdicts reproduce with no replacement, 88 changed paths with zero off-roster, reviewGuidance a pure append, Linux still in D-002 slice 1, and all 23 D-096 mentions refusals. Four repairs are complete. My own CLAUDE-V27-S1 is answered with both remedies — the Authenticode section walk is now written out with the SizeOfHeaders boundary, PointerToRawData sorting, SUM_OF_BYTES_HASHED accumulation, overlay handling and explicit gap exclusion, and specificationGoverns supplies the precedence sentence in the form I suggested, with new PE parse bounds and malformed-input refusals on top. Codex B1 is closed by a sealed-memfd snapshot taken before headerBind with every writable handle closed and all later stages confined to it, and the clause names the held-descriptor defect in its own words. B3 is closed by moving both consumption records to a single top-level location with a pathless associationToken derivation. S2 is closed by exact TPMS_ATTEST validation, a composite pcrDigest in ascending index order, an AK Name derived from the retained TPMT_PUBLIC and matched to qualifiedSigner, a four-field signedEntry, and a capped canonical nonce framing. The boot-time half of B2 is closed too, and closed well: the Calling action must sit at exactly logIndex minus 1, the kernel device path must equal the BootCurrent FilePathList, no other application event may intervene before the separator, and every pre-kernel code-bearing event must match a signed TCB member. What remains is the interval that begins where all of that evidence ends. Every proof in the bind is a boot-time fact, and the quote's freshness establishes only that the quote was taken during this run, not that the kernel is unchanged since boot — a PCR cannot be reset without a platform reset and a post-boot kernel transition extends nothing, so the log still replays, the composite still matches and the signature still verifies while different kernel bytes execute. The contract nonetheless declares its subject as 'kind: exactly running-kernel-package' with a digest of the running-kernel package bytes, never uses the phrase booted kernel, lists no post-boot condition in inScopeBootConfigs, refusesBootConfigs or unavailableRefuses, and contains zero occurrences of kexec, lockdown, continuity, since boot, boot_id, reboot, uptime or replacement. The OS-time adversary is inside the contract's own threat model, since excludesSyntheticExtend was written to defeat one. The result is a positive attestation naming a kernel that need not be running, which is why it is rated as a blocker rather than as the fail-closed findings of the last two rounds. Either constraining the interval or narrowing the declared subject to the kernel the boot manager launched closes it, and everything else in the ceremony should be kept verbatim.
